clue.text: A French the German stomachs in digs

parts.note: the French for 'a' (masculine) is un
der is the German masculine 'the'
to stomach something is to tolerate or bear it, so stomachs means stands

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and a German put up with sharing lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' looks like lodgings, but here it is slang for grasps or appreciates.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, someone who digs an idea follows and appreciates it: a synonym.

clue.text: Following the cross in ten up

indicators.note: the cross goes in, inside the turned word
in a down clue, up means the word ten is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Someone tracing a cross on a ten-sided figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TEN into NET, and 'in' puts X inside it between E and T.
explanation.definitionFit: What is next comes after, so it is the one following in order: a synonym.

clue.text: Eat in, fetch me some or eat out

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the words fetch me are used, a run sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A diner choosing between eating at home, takeaway, or going out.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run inside 'fetch me'. 'or eat out' is a second, looser definition: acid etches by eating out the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to corrode a surface with acid, which eats into the metal.

clue.text: They mind models easy targets

definitions.meaning: people who pose for a painter or photographer
in sport, a simple chance that should not be missed

explanation.surface: Babysitters looking after children who model, or are soft touches.
explanation.definitionFit: Childminders, artists' poseurs and sporting gifts are all called by the same noun in British usage.

clue.text: Greek contest past the point

parts.note: something past happened some time ago
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek competition that has long lost its relevance.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a public contest for a prize at games or festivals had this name, a borrowed term.

clue.text: Sued Ann for upsetting chaperones

indicators.note: upsetting the letters of Sued Ann tips them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sued Ann for overturning something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Older women employed to watch over young ladies in Spain and Portugal were known by this word: a synonym.

clue.text: Observe there is no inducement

indicators.note: the clue says the word for observe has no NO in it, so those two letters are taken away

parts.note: to observe something is to notice it

explanation.surface: A claim that nothing is being offered as a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: Take NO from NOTICE, leaving the archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for an enticement or lure, shortened from entice.

clue.text: She has the stomach to be an erotic entertainer

definitions.text: She has the stomach to be an erotic entertainer

parts.words: She has the stomach to be an erotic entertainer
parts.note: having the stomach usually means the nerve, but this performer literally dances with her midriff on show

explanation.surface: A woman with the courage to take up a racy stage career.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer whose sensuous act is built around rolling and shaking the abdomen.

clue.text: Say this father to father

definitions.meaning: a word one says when addressing a king, and also a male parent, especially of a horse

explanation.surface: Advice on what to call your dad.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an old form of address to royalty or a stallion parent, and a verb meaning beget.

clue.text: Ko-ko was high as this lord!

definitions.text: Ko-ko was high as this lord!

parts.words: Ko-ko was high as this lord!
parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera The Mikado, Ko-Ko holds the title Lord High ... of Titipu, the man who carries out sentences of death

explanation.surface: Ko-Ko was as drunk as a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests 'drunk as a lord'; the real reference is Ko-Ko's job title in The Mikado.
explanation.definitionFit: Ko-Ko's office in The Mikado is the one who carries out death sentences.

clue.text: Number of lambs born on the hill

definitions.meaning: in sheep farming, the crop of lambs born in a season
in northern England a high stretch of moorland or a mountain

explanation.surface: A farmer counting new lambs out on the hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the' links the two definitions. A fell is a hill in the Lake District and northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a season's crop of lambs and a moorland mountain in northern England.

clue.text: Lock keeper has a shock in store

definitions.text: Lock keeper has a shock in store

parts.words: Lock keeper has a shock in store
parts.note: a lock of hair and a shock of hair are both tufts; the person who looks after them has a salon

explanation.surface: A canal lock-keeper is about to get a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a canal official; 'lock' and 'shock' are both quantities of hair, and the 'store' is a salon.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylist who cuts and sets hair looks after locks and shocks in a shop.

clue.text: German made to go into the trough

indicators.note: the letters of German are made to go into a different order

explanation.surface: A German is forced into a feeding trough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into the' joins the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A long open box for animal feed in a stable: a synonym.

clue.text: Romantic confession of Conservative

parts.note: a confession of being something begins 'I am a', so the confession gives am a
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative admits to a passionate nature.
explanation.walkthrough: The confession reads '(I) am a Tory'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relating to love and desire is romantic in the sense of loving.

clue.text: These stories are spun all right

definitions.text: These stories are spun all right

parts.words: These stories are spun all right
parts.note: tall tales are spun, and thread is literally spun from fibre

explanation.surface: A comment that these stories are certainly being spun.
explanation.definitionFit: Both long tales and spun threads share the same noun.

clue.text: Stick with the old battleaxe

parts.note: a long staff bearing an axe head, as a medieval weapon

explanation.surface: Advice to stay loyal to a formidable old wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battleaxe' suggests a fearsome woman; here it is literal, a staff fitted with an axe blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval weapon that is a long pole topped by an axe blade and spike.

clue.text: Warms up for preliminary races

definitions.meaning: early rounds in athletics before the final

explanation.surface: Athletes loosening up before the first rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for making hot and the name for qualifying rounds.

clue.text: Struggles with experts losing polish capital

indicators.note: the word experts loses a letter, so it is taken out
a capital is a first letter, so this takes the opening of polish

explanation.surface: Struggles with experts who lose the Polish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polish capital' is P; the capital letter disguises it as Warsaw.
explanation.definitionFit: One exerts oneself in striving hard, so the verb sits close to struggles.

clue.text: Where lots go for small beers

parts.note: ales are beers

explanation.surface: Someone ordering many small beers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' suggests 'many'; it means auction lots. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Items at auction are lots, and they go under the hammer at auctions.

clue.text: Its popular to blow a fuse, that's cool

explanation.surface: Losing your temper is now fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a fury, and also a fashion craze, as in 'all the' craze.

clue.text: Aquatic bird on three-masted schooner

definitions.meaning: a seabird related to the gull
a sailing ship with three masts is named after a set of three

explanation.surface: A seabird perched on a sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' links the definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a gull-like seabird and, from a set of three, a three-masted schooner.

clue.text: Fits of bad temper a fool has aboard ship

indicators.note: being aboard a ship means inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a nit is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: A fool on board ship keeps losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fits of pique or irritation: a synonym.

clue.text: Guard who may betray one in front of the queen

indicators.note: these pieces come in front of the queen's letters

parts.note: to sell someone out is to betray them
I is the Roman numeral for one
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A palace guard who might betray the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who may' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard is one military member on duty: a soldier stands guard.

clue.text: A bird box dispute

parts.note: to spar is to box
a row is a dispute

explanation.surface: An argument over a bird box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' looks like a nest box; it is the verb to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown songbird, common in gardens: an example of a bird.

clue.text: Prepared rose-red altar screen

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters of rose-red are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rose-red screen made ready for a church altar.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental screen behind a church altar: a synonym.

clue.text: Doubtful respect for such an apparition

indicators.note: doubtful shows the letters of respect are not in their settled order

explanation.surface: A ghost that commands little respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for such an' links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost or phantom: a synonym.

clue.text: Barge into a point of intimidation

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
to cow is to intimidate

explanation.surface: Barging into someone as a means of bullying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barge' looks like a verb; it is the flat-bottomed boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed boat used for freight: a kind of barge.

clue.text: Norse deity making duck noise

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, O
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A Norse god quacking like a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief god in Norse mythology, father of Thor.

clue.text: Say, is that a Greek shield?

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as does say
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question asking whether an object is a Greek shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of aegis, the shield of Zeus or Athena in Greek myth.

clue.text: Help get water back to desert

indicators.note: help gets water in it, so one is placed inside the other

parts.note: aid is help
R stands for river, a body of water

explanation.surface: Help bringing water back to the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry land that receives little rain is what a desert is.

clue.text: The point now to ship cocaine

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
taken as written

explanation.surface: The moment has come to smuggle drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ship' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the drug, from its white powder look.

clue.text: Dab handed according to the record

definitions.text: Dab handed according to the record

parts.words: Dab handed according to the record
parts.note: a dab is slang for a mark left by a fingertip, and the police take it from the hand to put on file

explanation.surface: A skilled expert, as the record shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dab hand' suggests an expert; 'dab' is slang for the police's inked impression of a fingertip.
explanation.definitionFit: Police slang calls the ridged impression left by a fingertip a dab.

clue.text: Polish by the turn of the tide

indicators.note: turning the word tide round reads it backwards

explanation.surface: Polishing things up as the tide turns.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit copy is to polish and refine it.

clue.text: They have lost their husband playing with Swiss war god

indicators.note: playing with the letters of Swiss war god shuffles them

explanation.surface: Wives deserted while their men play with a Swiss god of war.
explanation.walkthrough: These wives haven't lost husbands to death: the men are temporarily away.
explanation.definitionFit: Wives whose husbands are often away from home for work or sport are called so in British usage.
